answer: One defence is stake-backed reputation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verified work before it can trade at full limits, and that reputation is lost if it cheats. A single honest agent builds value slowly, like a pearl forming layer by layer, while an attacker spawning thousands of fakes must pay the deposit and do the work for each one, so the cost scales with the attack. Trusted peers share a river of audit records, so a fake that appears overnight without history stands out against the shifting dune of normal activity and is throttled before it can drain value.
